message.reasoning:
I am ready to play Monopoly and make a decision.

I am p2 with $2,211 and three hotels on my properties. The opponent has only $16 and owns several other hotels. I have two get-out-of-jail cards.

I just collected $200 for passing GO. I am weighing whether to end my turn, propose a trade, unmortgage a property, or sell houses. The main threat is the opponent's Park Place and Boardwalk hotels.

Boardwalk hotel rent is $2,000 and Park Place hotel rent is $1,500. I can afford either with my current cash. Selling a pink hotel would yield about half its cost.

I am reconsidering the value of selling a pink hotel. Standard rules suggest it yields half the house cost, roughly $50, not the previously estimated $970.

Selling all pink hotels would raise about $750. The prior strategy is sound: keep the pink hotels to drain the opponent, leave PRR and Tennessee unmortgaged, avoid trading cash or get-out-of-jail cards, and end the turn.

I am on GO. Rolling a 6 lands on Oriental with its hotel rent at $550. Rolling an 8 lands on Vermont with the same rent. Both are light blue hotels.

Connecticut hotel rent is $600. I can pay all light blue hotels with my current cash. The opponent cannot land on dark blue hotels this turn because the maximum roll is 12 and those spaces are 37 and 39 spaces away. I am now mapping the opponent's possible moves from Kentucky Avenue.

The opponent's possible moves from Kentucky Avenue are now mapped. They can land on Indiana, Illinois, B&O Railroad, Atlantic Avenue, Ventnor Avenue, Water Works, Go to Jail, Pacific Avenue, or North Carolina Avenue. Most of these spaces are mortgaged and pay no rent.

The opponent cannot land on my pink hotels this turn. St. Charles Place is 30 spaces away from Kentucky Avenue, so they would need to pass GO and collect $200 before reaching it. After passing GO, they would have $216. My pink hotels are worth about $750 each.

Virginia hotel rent is $900. The opponent has hotels on light blues and dark blues plus houses on browns. Selling a hotel returns half its purchase price, leaving four houses behind. Fully liquidating requires selling all houses.

Full liquidation of all buildings would raise about $1,425. Adding the $16 cash brings the total to roughly $1,441. If the opponent passes GO first, they would have about $200 more before reaching the pinks. A $750 pink hotel hit would force them to sell some buildings, which would damage their dark blue hotels significantly.

Unmortgaging PRR would cost $110, but the opponent already owns the other three railroads and collects only $25 in rent. The opponent cannot pay any rent without selling buildings, so I will end my turn.

Unmortgaging Tennessee would cost $99 and break my orange monopoly. Trading it would complete the opponent's set. Selling a pink hotel is unnecessary because $2,211 already covers the $2,000 Boardwalk rent.

I am evaluating trade offers. Giving away a get-out-of-jail card would help the opponent avoid jail, which is not useful. The opponent will not trade away their dark blue hotels for anything I can offer. Mortgaged properties from other colors are useless without the full set. Their light blue hotels are affordable, but they do not help me much.

A deceptive trade offer would waste a turn and give the opponent information. The best action is to end the turn.
